subject.title: RFC: Readiness Providers and Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw own readiness providers and standard hosting profiles as durable core plugin, configuration, and release-support contracts?
rationale: The proposal deliberately creates permanent public API, persisted configuration, operational semantics, and release-testing commitments that technical review alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Review the full contract
options.body: Evaluate and calibrate the provider API, profile catalog, upgrade defaults, and conformance matrix as one coordinated direction.

options.title: Accept a narrower foundation
options.body: Advance canonical readiness normalization while deferring provider registration and hosting-profile composition.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Leave hosting-specific readiness composition downstream and close the RFC after documenting that direction.

recommendation.title: Review the full contract
recommendation.body: Evaluate and calibrate the provider API, profile catalog, upgrade defaults, and conformance matrix as one coordinated direction.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the repository's acceptance and maintainer-discussion process and are the strongest evidence-backed routing owner for advancing this RFC decision.
